summary: This benchmark evaluates a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy that adds reversible, single-expert plug-ins to each layer of frozen OLMoE-1B-7B. The study rigorously compares the approach against parameter-matched attention LoRA, full fine-tuning, and router ablations across matched token budgets, demonstrating high gain recovery alongside honest reporting of out-of-domain degradation and cross-plug-in interference.
strengths: Rigorous, apples-to-apples experimental controls including parameter-matched attention LoRA (100.7M parameters) and token-matched full fine-tuning.
Pre-registered evaluation criteria and transparent reporting of negative results, such as the 2.34% Python validation loss increase exceeding the registered 1% retention limit.
Comprehensive verification of reversibility, confirming bit-identical logit restoration upon module removal.
Exploration of multi-plug-in interference when installing two independently trained language experts simultaneously.
weaknesses: Evaluation is restricted to cross-entropy validation loss on fixed windows rather than downstream task or generation benchmarks.
Single random seed and single base checkpoint (OLMoE-1B-7B-0924), leaving statistical variance unquantified across runs.
Bit-identical logit restoration was evaluated on only two fixed windows, which is a small sample for numerical drift testing.
suggestions: Evaluate downstream generation quality or standard NLP benchmark tasks (e.g., translation, question answering) in addition to perplexity/loss.
Expand validation of bit-identical output restoration to a broader test corpus across different sequence lengths and batch sizes.
Run multiple training seeds to provide confidence intervals for the gain recovery percentages and retention degradations.

claims.text: OLMoE has 16 layers of 64 experts with eight selected per token.
Adding experts for continued learning has precedent in Lifelong-MoE
Branch-Train-MiX combines independently trained branches and then trains routing.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Lifelong Language Pretraining with Distribution-Specialized Experts
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies modular expert expansion to a modern open-weight sparse MoE architecture (OLMoE) with exact bit-level reversibility upon detachment and measures cross-expert routing interference.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Branch-Train-MiX: Mixing Expert LLMs into a Mixture-of-Experts LLM
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses on lightweight, detachable modular plug-ins per layer without full model branching and retraining, specifically analyzing retention limits and out-of-domain degradation.
